info.title: Mailcheer API
info.summary: Transactional email, subscribers, suppression lists and campaigns.

servers.description: Production. There is no separate test environment: try it on a workspace of your own, with an address of your own. Every path below already includes the `/api/v1` prefix.

get.description: No key required: lists the endpoints, the permissions and the address of the documentation.

The domain that carries the links and pixel of the workspace's emails (`click.your-domain.com`), its status and the DNS records to add. `hostname` is `null` until one is declared. No particular permission is required.

status.description: pending_dns, verifying, issuing_certificate, active or failed.

links_origin.description: The address that links and the pixel of new emails carry today.

post.description: `{ "hostname": "click.your-domain.com" }`, or `{}` for the name suggested from a verified sending domain. Then add the CNAME to `clients.clickmailcheer.com` (DNS only): the domain becomes active as soon as a real HTTPS request comes back through it. Requires `emails:send`.

status.description: pending_dns, verifying, issuing_certificate, active or failed.

links_origin.description: The address that links and the pixel of new emails carry today.

409.description: The workspace already has a tracking domain, or the name is taken.

get.description: Workspace, the key's permissions, plan, this month's usage (sent, queued, remaining, reset date), billing status and any scheduled plan change, member and domain limits, the daily limit of a new workspace, sending domains and senders. Call this first: it is what tells you which address to write from — and, before a send, whether it fits. No particular permission is required.

post.description:
Permission required: `emails:send`.

Answers **202**: Amazon has accepted the message, it is not delivered yet. Delivery is confirmed a few seconds later with `GET /api/v1/emails/{id}`.

Use the `Idempotency-Key` header: replaying a successful call returns the same response without a second send, for 24 hours. A refusal is not kept: once its cause is lifted, the same call with the same key goes out.

An address that unsubscribed from the workspace receives an individual email; with `unsubscribe_url`, the send is a newsletter or prospecting and is refused to it (`422 suppressed_recipient`). A bounce, a complaint or a manual suppression refuses both.

With a test key (`mch_test_…`), the same checks and the same response — but nothing goes out and the quota is not touched; events are simulated. See Test mode.

value.subject: Your September invoice
value.html: Here it is, attached to this message.

Idempotent-Replay.description: `true` if the response is that of an identical call already handled.

accepte.summary: Accepted — read it again a few seconds later

get.description: Permission required: `emails:send`. The status changes after the send, as our provider reports back. With a test key, only test emails are found; a live key never sees them.

post.summary: Verify addresses before writing to them
post.description: Checks one address (`email`) or up to 100 (`emails`) without sending anything: syntax, a domain that receives mail, a mailbox that already hard-bounced on Mailcheer, disposable and role mailboxes, and DNS signals of a dead mailbox. No SMTP probe: `valid` means nothing known stands against the address, not that the mailbox exists. Limit: 20,000 addresses per workspace per day. Requires `emails:send`.

200.description: One verification for `email`, a list with `summary` for `emails`.

verdict.description: invalid: writing to it will bounce · risky: may bounce, or is not a person · unknown: DNS did not answer in time · valid: nothing known stands against it.

mail_provider.description: The mail provider recognized from the MX records (google, microsoft, ovh-mxplan…), or null.

suppressed.description: The reason, if the address is on this workspace's suppression list.

suppressed.description: The reason, if the address is on this workspace's suppression list.

get.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:read`.

`updated_since` returns only the records created or changed since that date.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search on address, first name or last name.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: ISO 8601. Only the records created or changed since then — status, name, fields, tags. Keep the largest `updated_at` you receive and pass it next time, minus one minute: you catch up without reading the whole list.

post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`.

By default the person enters `pending` and receives a confirmation email. `double_opt_in: false` subscribes them straight away — to be used only if consent was collected elsewhere, and the caller then bears responsibility for it.

An address on the suppression list, unsubscribed, or returned as a hard bounce is refused.

simple.summary: An address and a first name

200.description: The subscriber already existed and has been updated.

post.summary: Add or update up to 500 subscribers
post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`.

Each entry goes through exactly the same path as `POST /api/v1/subscribers`: double opt-in by default, the confirmation guard, the suppression list, unsubscribed people who are not brought back. A refused line does not fail the others: the response gives one line per entry, in order — `created`, `updated` or `rejected` with the refusal the single add would have returned. The same address twice in a batch: the second is rejected.

A batch of N counts as N requests against the rate limit (600 per minute per key): it saves round trips, it does not raise the limit. A refused batch consumes nothing (`429`, `Retry-After`).

lot.summary: Two people whose consent was collected elsewhere

delete.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`.

**Does not erase the record**: the person moves to `unsubscribed` and their address enters the suppression list. Erasing the trace would bring the address back at the next file import. The person no longer receives your campaigns, your automations, or sends carrying `unsubscribe_url`; your individual emails still reach them.

post.summary: Add or remove tags on one subscriber
post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`.

Changes the record's tags and nothing else: no subscription, no confirmation email, no status touched — unlike `POST /api/v1/subscribers`, which is a subscription and sends the confirmation again to a `pending` person. The record must exist (`404` otherwise; nothing is created). Idempotent: adding a tag already there, or removing one that is absent, is not an error; `added` and `removed` say what really changed. A new tag is created.

add.description: Tags to put on the record.

post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`. **Irreversible.**

The right to erasure: the record, the name, the custom fields, the proof of consent and the tags are deleted. What was promised and not sent will not be sent; automation journeys stop. The statistics of campaigns already sent do not move — each message stays counted, with nothing left that links it to the person.

Distinct from `DELETE /api/v1/subscribers/{email}`, which unsubscribes and KEEPS the record so the address does not come back at the next import. The suppression list is not touched: an address on it stays there (`suppressed: true`), which is what guarantees nothing is sent to it again. Removing an address from that list is done by hand, in the workspace.

get.description: Permission required: `subscribers:read`. Every tag of the workspace, by name, with the number of subscribers carrying it and, among them, the active ones.

patch.description: Permission required: `subscribers:write`. Subscribers keep the tag under its new name; segments, automations and forms point to it by `id` and see nothing change. A name already taken by another tag: `409` — merging two tags is not renaming.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: The tag's `id`, or its name URL-encoded (`clients%20VIP`).

delete.description: Permission required: `subscribers:write`. The SUBSCRIBERS stay as they are: only the tag is taken off them. Refused (`409`) while an automation, a segment or a signup form uses it — without it they would carry on silently, reaching nobody; `details.used_by` names them.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: The tag's `id`, or its name URL-encoded (`clients%20VIP`).

post.summary: Add or remove a tag on many subscribers
post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`.

Puts the tag on the addresses in `add` and removes it from those in `remove` — up to 500 of each, in one call. No subscription, no email, no status touched. An unknown address is returned in `not_found`, never created. The tag is created if `add` names it and it does not exist yet; for a removal alone, it must exist (`404`).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: The tag's `id`, or its name URL-encoded (`clients%20VIP`).

get.description: Permission required: `subscribers:read`. The `scope` field distinguishes addresses suppressed for this workspace (`organization`) from those suppressed platform-wide (`platform`). `reason` says what the entry refuses: `unsubscribe` refuses campaigns, automations and sends carrying `unsubscribe_url`; `bounce`, `complaint` and `manual` refuse everything, individual emails included.

post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:write`. The matching subscriber, if there is one, moves to `unsubscribed` in the same operation. Without `reason`, the entry is `manual` and refuses everything, individual emails included; `unsubscribe` only refuses campaigns, automations and sends carrying `unsubscribe_url`. An entry already `bounce`, `complaint` or `manual` is never downgraded to `unsubscribe`.

**No endpoint removes an address from this list**, and that is deliberate: it is the one action that suspends a sending capability. It is done by hand, in your Mailcheer workspace.

Permission required: `campaigns:write`. **Nothing goes out**: sending is a second action, deliberately kept separate.

Content is written either in blocks (`content`) or in plain text (`text`): a blank line separates two paragraphs, `# ` at the start of a line makes a heading.

texte.summary: A letter written in plain text

value.name: September newsletter
value.subject: What we changed this month
value.preheader: Three new things, and one we owed you.
value.text:
# Three new things

Here is what changed this month.

Enjoy the read.

get.description: Permission required: `campaigns:read`. Rates are calculated on delivered messages, not on recipients: a dead address must not pull down the open rate of those who did receive it. `open_rate` and `click_rate` include bots, as most tools count them; `human_open_rate` and `human_click_rate` set them aside.

patch.description: Permission required: `campaigns:write`. Changes a campaign with status `draft`: name, subject, preheader, kind, sender, content (`content` in blocks, or `text`). Nothing is sent. Any other status answers 409 `conflict` with the current status in `details.status`, and nothing is changed: what is scheduled, sending or sent is not rewritten.

value.subject: What we changed this month
value.text:
# Three new things

Here is what changed.

200.description: The draft, as it is now.

409.description: Not a draft: nothing was changed.

delete.description: Permission required: `campaigns:write`. Only a campaign with status `draft` can be deleted. Any other status (`scheduled`, `sending`, `testing`, `sent`, `archived`) answers 409 `conflict` with the current status in `details.status`: a campaign that has sent, or will send, keeps its figures. Deleting a draft cannot be undone.

409.description: Not a draft: nothing was deleted.

get.description: Permission required: `campaigns:read`. Everything the Mailcheer campaign view shows, so you can display it in your own software: counters, rates (shares between 0 and 1, `null` as long as nothing has gone out), the curve of the first 48 hours in eight six-hour windows (empty if the campaign has not gone out), what people read on (top five rows, shares between 0 and 1, `proxiedShare` = the share of opens coming from a privacy relay such as Apple Mail or Gmail), links from most to least clicked, and the HTML as rendered at send time (empty string otherwise). Every figure comes twice: bots included (`opened`, `clicked` — as most tools count) and without bots (`humanOpened`, `humanClicked`), with `bots` saying how many were set aside and why. Open and click rates are calculated on delivered messages; delivery and bounce rates on recipients.

Permission required: `campaigns:read`. Who the campaign went to and what each person did with it: delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained, unsubscribed. Cursor pagination, like `/subscribers`. `opened_at` and `clicked_at` include bots (security gateways, privacy relays); `human_opened` and `human_clicked` say whether a PERSON opened or clicked. `email` is `null` when the contact was deleted after the send: the row stays, because it still counts in the campaign's figures. `unsubscribed` is an attribution: the person unsubscribed after this email and before receiving another one (the unsubscribe link identifies the person, not the campaign). Cancelled messages are not recipients and are left out.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter. `opened` and `clicked` include bots; `not_opened`: sent, not bounced, never opened.

unsubscribed.description: Unsubscribed through THIS email's link. Emails sent before 2026-09-24, whose link only identified the person: attributed to the last email received before the unsubscribe.

post.description:
Permission required: `campaigns:write`. **Irreversible** (except `dry_run`).

⚠️ **Without a body, the campaign goes to ALL subscribers of its audience with status `subscribed`** (the whole list, or the segment chosen in the interface) — minus those on the suppression list, recomputed at the last moment.

**`to` restricts the send to a list of addresses.** It can only narrow: the letter goes to the requested addresses that are active subscribers of the audience, never to an address on the suppression list. The response carries `audience`: who is kept, who is excluded, and why. An empty list writes to nobody (422); a campaign with an A/B test refuses `to` (the winning version would go out later to the whole audience).

**`dry_run: true` runs every check and queues nothing**: a `200` response with `would_send`, `blocked_reason` and the recipient count. That is the number to show BEFORE confirming. Other fields are ignored, as before — except look-alikes of `dry_run` (`dryRun`, `dry-run`, `test`, `simulate`…) and of `to` (`To`, `recipients`, `emails`, `to_emails`, `destinataires`, `audience`…), refused with 422: ignored, the former would send for real, the latter would send to the whole list.

The call freezes the recipient list and fills the queue. Messages then go out at the rate our provider allows: the response says `sending` and a `queued` count, never `sent`. Follow the progress with `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}`.

A campaign already `sending` or `sent` returns 409: we do not re-send, we duplicate. An insufficient monthly quota, a workspace with damaged reputation, no sender, or an empty list return 422 with the reason.

to.description: Optional. Restricts the send to these addresses — only those that are active subscribers of the audience, never an address on the suppression list. Omitted: the whole audience. Empty (`[]`): nobody, the send is refused.

dry_run.description: `true`: check and count everything, queue nothing.

would_send.description: Would the real send, started now, go out?

blocked_reason.description: If not, the exact message the real send would return.

recipients.description: How many would be queued; `null` if the refusal comes before counting.

audience.description: The per-address breakdown, when `to` is given.

queued.description: The number of recipients actually frozen in the queue.

audience.description: Present when the send was restricted by `to`.

note.description: What is left to happen, in plain words. Written for a human; do not write logic against it.

value.note: 3182 recipient(s) queued. Messages then go out at the rate our sending provider allows; follow the progress with GET /v1/campaigns/cmp_8d2.

post.summary: Who would receive, without creating a campaign
post.description:
Permission required: `subscribers:read`. **Read-only**: nothing is created, nothing is sent.

Returns what a campaign sent right now to the whole list would reach — restricted to `to` if given, with the same per-address breakdown as the send. To display "12 will receive, 3 are excluded" while someone chooses who to write to, without creating a draft.

Campaign-specific checks (subject, content, quota, segment) remain those of `dry_run` on `POST /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/send`.

to.description: Optional. Restricts the send to these addresses — only those that are active subscribers of the audience, never an address on the suppression list. Omitted: the whole audience. Empty (`[]`): nobody, the send is refused.

200.description: The recipient count, and the per-address breakdown if `to` is given.

get.description: Permission required: `webhooks:read`. Secrets do not appear in the list — read the subscription itself to get one.

post.description: Permission required: `webhooks:write`. The response carries the `secret` — store it like a password, it is what verifies every call.

get.description: Permission required: `webhooks:read`. The secret is readable, unlike an API key: it gives access to nothing on our side, and a service being redeployed needs it to verify signatures.

patch.description: Permission required: `webhooks:write`. Pass `enabled: false` to suspend without losing the log.

delete.description: Permission required: `webhooks:write`. The delivery log goes with it.

post.description: Permission required: `webhooks:write`. Same signature, same headers, same log as a real event — and your service's response is AWAITED, so you know straight away. The body carries `"data": { "test": true }`.

get.description: Permission required: `webhooks:read`. This is what answers “I am not receiving anything”: you see the attempt, the status code your service returned and the start of its response.

parameters.name: deliveryId
parameters.description: The identifier of the delivery to replay.

post.description: Permission required: `webhooks:write`. The replayed body is the original one, byte for byte — so the same event `id`. If your service had in fact received it, it will recognize a duplicate.

post.summary: An email sent through the API went out
post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.sent` when our sending provider accepts an email sent through the API (`POST /api/v1/emails`, MCP `send_email`), one event per address — `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, told apart by `recipient_type`. API emails only (`source: "api"`); campaign emails do not produce it. With a test key, it arrives marked `"test": true`. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }`: check `data.test` first.

2XX.description: Any 2xx within 15 seconds acknowledges receipt. Anything else — another status, a redirect (not followed), no answer, a network error — is retried: 5 attempts in all, the next ones 30 s, 2 min, 10 min and 1 h after the previous failure.

post.summary: An email sent through the API did not go out
post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.failed` when an email sent through the API was recorded but did not go out — the status `failed` of `GET /api/v1/emails/{id}` — one event per address. `reason` says why: `provider_rejected`, `safety_review`, `suspended` or `interrupted`. A refusal that recorded nothing (quota, domain, suppression list…) produces no event: there is no email, only an error response. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }`: check `data.test` first.

2XX.description: Any 2xx within 15 seconds acknowledges receipt. Anything else — another status, a redirect (not followed), no answer, a network error — is retried: 5 attempts in all, the next ones 30 s, 2 min, 10 min and 1 h after the previous failure.

post.summary: The recipient's mail server accepted the email
post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.delivered` when the recipient's mail server accepts the email. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.opened` when the email is opened — the tracking pixel loaded, robots included, like `opened_at`. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.clicked` when a link in the email is clicked; `data.url` says which. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.bounced` when the email bounces; `data.reason` gives the type. A `Permanent` bounce adds the address to the suppression list. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.summary: The recipient marked the email as spam
post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.complained` when the recipient marks the email as spam. The address joins the suppression list. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `email.received` when a recipient replies on `reply.<your domain>` — only for a domain where reply receiving is turned on (the domain's screen in the app, one MX record). The whole reply is in the body except attachments, which come as signed download links valid for 7 days. Replies over 150 KB are refused by Amazon and never arrive. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) can arrive under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `subscriber.created` when a subscriber is added: signup form (`source: form`), API or MCP (`source: api`), or by hand in the app (`source: manual`). Confirming a `pending` subscriber produces no event. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

2XX.description: Any 2xx within 15 seconds acknowledges receipt. Anything else — another status, a redirect (not followed), no answer, a network error — is retried: 5 attempts in all, the next ones 30 s, 2 min, 10 min and 1 h after the previous failure.

post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `subscriber.unsubscribed` when a subscriber leaves: the unsubscribe link of an email, the API or MCP, or the app. A bounce or a complaint does not produce it; the same person can be reported more than once — handle it as idempotent. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

post.summary: The monthly quota reached a threshold
post.description: Posted to the subscriptions to `quota.threshold_reached` at 50, 80, 95 and 100% of the monthly quota, once a month per threshold. Signed and retried like every event. The test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`) arrives under this `type` too, with `data: { test: true, message }` and none of the fields of the real event: check `data.test` first.

bearerAuth.description:
An API key for the workspace, created under Settings → API in your Mailcheer workspace. Shape: `mch_live_…` — or `mch_test_…` for a test key, which checks everything and sends nothing (see Test mode).

`Authorization: Bearer mch_live_…`

The key carries permissions (`scopes`): every operation states which one it requires, and `GET /api/v1/me` states the ones yours carries. A key belongs to ONE workspace — there is no cross-workspace call.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same key, in a dedicated header. Strictly equivalent to the Bearer form: some enterprise clients and gateways do not let `Authorization` through. Do not send both.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Number of items per page, from 1 to 100.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A unique value per send. Replaying a successful call (2xx) returns the same response, without a second send, for 24 hours after the first call. A refusal (402, 422, 423, 429…) is not kept: once its cause is lifted, send the same call with the same key and it goes out. The same key with a different body returns 409 `idempotency_key_reused`; an identical call still in progress, 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`.

Mailcheer-Signature.name: Mailcheer-Signature
Mailcheer-Signature.description: `t=<unix timestamp>,v1=<hex>`: `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `"<t>.<raw body>"` keyed with the subscription's secret. Reject a `t` more than 300 seconds away from your clock.

Mailcheer-Event-Id.name: Mailcheer-Event-Id
Mailcheer-Event-Id.description: The event's `id` — the same on every attempt and every replay: the deduplication key.

Mailcheer-Delivery-Id.name: Mailcheer-Delivery-Id
Mailcheer-Delivery-Id.description: This delivery. A manual replay gets a new one.

Mailcheer-Mode.description: `live`, or `test` when the call was made with a test key (`mch_test_…`): nothing is sent and the quota is not touched.

Mailcheer-Quota-Limit.description: Emails a month included in the workspace's plan, or `unlimited`.

Mailcheer-Quota-Used.description: Emails sent this month **plus** those waiting in the queue (campaigns being sent, API sends in progress). The same count as `usage.emails_sent + usage.emails_in_flight` in `GET /api/v1/me`.

Mailcheer-Quota-Remaining.description: What can still be sent this month, queue already deducted — never negative. `unlimited` on an unlimited plan.

Mailcheer-Quota-Reset.description: When the counter resets, in ISO 8601: the 1st of next month, 00:00 UTC.

Mailcheer-Key-Quota-Limit.description: Only for a key with a monthly limit: the limit set on THIS key (Settings → API). Absent otherwise.

Mailcheer-Key-Quota-Used.description: Only for a key with a monthly limit: what this key sent this month (its emails and the campaigns it launched), plus what is still queued.

Mailcheer-Key-Quota-Remaining.description: Only for a key with a monthly limit: what this key can still send this month — never negative. It resets with the workspace quota (`Mailcheer-Quota-Reset`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Present on EVERY `429` and every `423`.

EmailRequest.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/emails`.

`from`, `to` and `subject` are required, and **at least one of `html` or `text`** — an empty body is refused with a 422.

Attachments go in `attachments`, in Resend's format.

Unknown keys are silently ignored: a body written for Resend passes through as is.

from.description: **Required.** An address on a domain verified in the workspace — otherwise 422 `unverified_from_domain`, which hands you the list of domains you can use. `GET /api/v1/me` gives it too, before you try. Both forms are accepted: the bare address, or “Name <address@domain.com>” so the name shows in the inbox.

to.description:
**Required.** One recipient, or an array of 1 to 50 recipients. At most 50 addresses in all, `to`, `cc` and `bcc` together — our sending provider's limit per message; beyond, `422 validation_error`. Beyond 50, split into several calls — or go through a campaign. Each entry accepts the form “Name <address@domain.com>” as well as the bare address, and is 3 to 320 characters long.

⚠️ **Recipients see one another**: they go out in the same message, not as blind copies. For each to receive their own, make one call per person.

subject.description: **Required.** The message's subject. The 998-character ceiling is the email standard's; in practice an inbox shows 40 to 60.

html.description: The body in HTML. `html` or `text`: at least one of the two, both if you can — a message with no text version is marked down by filters.
examples: Here it is, attached to this message.

text.description: The body in plain text, for clients that do not display HTML.
examples: Here it is, attached to this message.

cc.description: Visible copy. One address or an array of 1 to 50. Recipients in copy see and are seen. They count against the quota and go through the same checks as `to` — suppression list included.

bcc.description: Blind copy. One address or an array of 1 to 50. It appears in no header of the received message, including when the send carries attachments — it stays in the envelope. Same quota and same checks as `to`.

replyTo.description: The address recipients will reply to, when it differs from `from`. One, or an array of 1 to 10. Same form as `to`: the bare address or “Name <address>”.

reply_to.description:
Alias of `replyTo`, for clients coming from Resend. The address recipients will reply to, when it differs from `from`. One, or an array of 1 to 10. Same form as `to`: the bare address or “Name <address>”.

Fill in only one of the two.

headers.description: Free-form headers, as name → value pairs. The ones that carry the message's identity (From, To, Reply-To, List-Unsubscribe…) are ignored: they are ours to answer for.

tags.description:
Free-form tags for your own tracking; they come back in delivery notifications and on `GET /api/v1/emails/{id}`. Two ways to write them: an object of key → value, or an array of `{name, value}` as with Resend (10 entries at most in that second form).

Names and values are **rewritten, not refused**: any character outside `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -` becomes `_`, and beyond 256 characters the value is cut. An accent or a space therefore passes without error, but not unchanged.

unsubscribe_url.description: The one-click unsubscribe address. Mailcheer then sets `List-Unsubscribe` AND `List-Unsubscribe-Post` — the two always go together, and without the second Gmail shows no button. Gmail and Yahoo have expected this header since February 2024 on any send to people who did not write to you first; without it, the only way out you offer is the Spam button, and it is your sending domain's reputation that pays. Must be https. The header itself is still rejected inside `headers`: Mailcheer writes it, you only provide the target. It also says what kind of send this is: with it, a newsletter or prospecting, refused to an address that unsubscribed; without it, an individual email, which an unsubscribe does not stop.

filename.description: The file name as it will appear in the inbox. Line breaks and path separators are stripped from it.

content.description: The file, encoded in **base64**. That is the only accepted form.

content_type.description: The MIME type. Optional: inferred from the extension when missing (`.pdf` → `application/pdf`), falling back to `application/octet-stream`.

content_id.description: Makes the attachment an **inline image**: reference it in the HTML with `cid:` (``). It goes out with a `Content-ID` header in a `multipart/related` part and shows in place instead of as a download. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, `@`, no spaces; unique within the message.

attachments.description:
Attachments, in Resend's format: `filename` + `content` in base64. Twenty at most.

**The limit is Amazon SES's: 40 MB per message once encoded**, which is roughly 30 MB of actual files (base64 adds a third). Beyond that the call is refused with a 422 naming the file, its size and the size reached — no message goes out without its attachment.

Rejected, and always out loud: extensions inbox providers reject (`.exe`, `.bat`, `.js`, `.vbs`…), a `content` that is not valid base64, and Resend's `path` field — our server will not fetch a file from an address you choose; encode it.

Without an attachment, nothing changes in the way the message goes out.

track_opens.description: Insert an open-tracking pixel (HTML body only). Omitted, your workspace's “Track opens” setting decides (the Workspace screen of the app); sent, it overrides that setting for this email. In France, the CNIL's recommendation of 14 April 2026 makes measuring opens with a pixel, to track campaign performance, subject to the recipient's prior consent.

track_clicks.description: Track clicks: the http(s) links of the <a> tags of the HTML go through your tracking domain. Left untouched: mailto:, tel:, anchors, unsubscribe_url and links carrying data-no-track. Without this field, the workspace's “Track clicks” setting decides — on by default, for every email, individual ones included. `false` leaves a message untouched. Login, verification and reset links (recognized by their address or a token) always stay untouched.

verify.description: Verify recipients before sending (same checks as `POST /api/v1/verify`). An `invalid` recipient refuses the entire call with `422 undeliverable_recipient`; `risky` and `unknown` addresses go out. Default false.

id.description: The identifier to pass back to `GET /api/v1/emails/{id}` to learn about delivery.

to.description: Always an array in the response, even if you passed a single address.

status.description: `queued` on acceptance, then `sent`, `delivered`, `opened`, `bounced`, `complained` or `failed` as our provider reports back. Expect a few seconds before `delivered`. With several addresses, it follows the recipients in `to` only: a copy (`cc`, `bcc`) that bounces does not change it — read `recipients` for each address.

error.description: The reason for the refusal, when `status` is `bounced`, `complained` or `failed`. `null` otherwise.

tags.description: The send's tags, after forbidden characters were rewritten.

open_count.description: How many times the tracking pixel was loaded. Apple and Gmail preload images: this says attention, not readings.

human_opened_at.description: The first open by a person — `null` as long as only bots have opened.

track_opens.description: Whether this email carried an open-tracking pixel. `false`: `opened_at` stays `null` because opens are not tracked, not because nobody opened.

track_clicks.description: Whether this email's links were tracked (`track_clicks`).

click_count.description: How many times a tracked link was clicked, bots included.

human_clicked_at.description: The first click by a person — `null` as long as only bots have clicked.

recipients.description: Every address of the email — `to`, then `cc`, then `bcc` — with what Amazon reported for it. `status` above follows `to` only; here each copy has its own state. Opens are not per address: the tracking pixel is the same in every copy.

status.description: `sent` until Amazon reports on this address, then `delivered`, `bounced` or `complained`. `queued` or `failed` while the email itself is.

reason.description: The bounce type Amazon reports (`Permanent`, `Transient`, `Undetermined`) when `status` is `bounced`. `null` otherwise.

prenom.description: Alias of `firstName`. Fill in only one of the two.

nom.description: Alias of `lastName`. Fill in only one of the two.

tags.description: Workspace tags. The ones that do not exist yet are created.

fields.description: Custom fields, by their technical key. Unknown keys create nothing: they come back in `ignored_fields`.

double_opt_in.description: `false` subscribes straight away, with no confirmation email. The caller then bears responsibility for the consent.

updated_at.description: The last change to the record: status, name, fields, tags. Keep the largest value you receive and pass it as `updated_since` next time, minus one minute.

confirmation_sent.description: `true` if a confirmation email went out with THIS call. Exactly when `confirmation_not_sent_reason` is `null`.

confirmation_not_sent_reason.description: Why no confirmation went out with this call: `not_needed` (already confirmed, or `double_opt_in: false`), `recently_sent` (one went out less than 2 minutes ago), `daily_limit` (3 per address per 24 hours, all channels combined), `send_failed` (the provider refused it; call again later). `null` when one went out.

confirmation_retry_at.description: When a new call can send one again (ISO 8601): set only for `recently_sent` and `daily_limit`, otherwise `null`.

ignored_fields.description: Keys of `fields` unknown to this workspace, written nowhere.

name.description: **Required.** Internal name, never seen by recipients.

subject.description: The subject. It may stay empty on a draft, but the send will refuse it.

preheader.description: Preview shown after the subject in the inbox.
examples: Three new things, and one we owed you.

kind.description: Your own classification label. Free text, no imposed value.

from.description: The address of a sender **already registered** in the workspace — not any address on a verified domain, unlike an individual send. Unknown: 404, with the list of available addresses. `GET /api/v1/me` gives them in `senders`.

sender_id.description:
The sender's identifier, if you know it (`senders[].id` from `GET /api/v1/me`). Takes precedence over `from`.

With neither `from` nor `sender_id`, Mailcheer takes the workspace's default sender; failing that, if a single sender exists, that one. If several exist with no default, the campaign is created **without a sender** and it is the send that will fail: designate one.

text.description: The content in plain text — the form to prefer from code or from an agent. A blank line separates two paragraphs, `# ` at the start of a line makes a heading, `## ` a subheading. Ignored if `content` is provided.
examples:
# Three new things

Here is what changed this month.

Enjoy the read.

content.description: The content in blocks, the editor's full form. Write this only if you are reusing the content of an existing campaign: to compose, `text` does the same job without your having to fabricate block identifiers.

blocks.description: Editor blocks, each with its `id` and its `type` (`heading`, `text`, …).

CampaignRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/v1/campaigns`. Only `name` is required — but a draft with no subject and no content cannot be sent. Give the content through `text` (plain) or through `content` (blocks), never both.

schedule_error.description: Why a scheduled send did not go out.

open_rate.description: Percentage of delivered messages opened at least once, one decimal — bots included, as most tools count it.

click_rate.description: Percentage of delivered messages clicked at least once, one decimal — bots included.

human_opened.description: Messages opened (or clicked) at least once by a person, bots set aside.

human_clicked.description: Messages clicked at least once by a person, bots set aside.

human_open_rate.description: `open_rate` without bots: the closest figure to real readings.

opens_tracked.description: `false` when every delivered message went out without an open-tracking pixel (the workspace's “Track opens” setting was off): `open_rate` and `human_open_rate` are then `null`. Open figures only count messages that carried the pixel.

stats.description: A bot is an open or a click within two minutes of delivery (security gateways visit every link as the message arrives; privacy relays preload images), or one from a robot that declares itself in its user agent or comes from an address range its operator publishes (Google, Bing). Privacy relays (Apple Mail, Gmail, Yahoo) are not bots in themselves.

humanOpened.description: Messages opened (or clicked) at least once by a person.

humanClicked.description: Messages clicked at least once by a person.

unsubscribed.description: People who unsubscribed through this campaign's link (same definition as `recipients?status=unsubscribed`). An unsubscribe made through the API or in the app counts on no campaign.

untracked.description: Delivered messages that went out without an open-tracking pixel. Open rates are computed on the others; with none left, they are `null`.

counts.description: A bot is an open or a click within two minutes of delivery (security gateways visit every link as the message arrives; privacy relays preload images), or one from a robot that declares itself in its user agent or comes from an address range its operator publishes (Google, Bing). Privacy relays (Apple Mail, Gmail, Yahoo) are not bots in themselves.

rates.description: Shares between 0 and 1; `null` as long as the denominator is empty.

bots.description: Opens and clicks set aside as bots, counted as events (a gateway visiting three links counts three clicks), and why.

scanner.description: A robot that declares itself, or an address its operator publishes.

timeline.description: Eight six-hour windows from the send, `+0h` to `+42h`. Empty if the campaign has not gone out.

humanOpened.description: Opens by people in the window.

humanClicked.description: Clicks by people in the window.

total.description: Opens by people whose device is known (bot opens excluded).

proxiedShare.description: Share of opens coming from a privacy relay (Apple Mail, Gmail): received, not necessarily read.

device.description: Five rows at most, from the most to the least frequent.

os.description: Five rows at most, from the most to the least frequent.

client.description: Five rows at most, from the most to the least frequent.

links.description: From most to least clicked, by people (bot clicks excluded).

html.description: The HTML as rendered at send time; empty string as long as it does not exist.

Audience.description: The breakdown of a send restricted by `to`. The count always adds up: `requested = duplicates + retained + excluded`.

duplicates.description: Entries repeating an address already seen (case and spaces ignored).

retained.description: Addresses that receive (or would receive) the campaign.

reasons.description: Excluded addresses per reason; every reason is present, even at zero.

not_in_list.description: No subscriber of the workspace has this address.

suppressed.description: Active subscriber, but the address is on the suppression list.

outside_segment.description: Active subscriber, outside the segment the campaign targets.

excluded_addresses.description: Every excluded address, with its reason.

Account.description: What the key gives access to, and what is left to use. The first call to make: it gives the verified domains and the registered senders — that is, the only addresses your sends will pass with — and everything a send can be refused for: the monthly quota (queue included), the daily limit of a new workspace, the billing status.

organization.description: The workspace the key belongs to. `null` if the workspace has been deleted.

key.description: The key used for this call. Its secret is never returned.

id.description: The key's identifier (not its secret) — the `key_id` of a `key_quota_exceeded`.

scopes.description: The permissions of THIS key. A call outside this list returns 403.

mode.description: `live`, or `test` for a test key (`mch_test_…`): its sends are checked and simulated, nothing goes out.

language.description: The language of this key's messages when a call asks for none (`Accept-Language` absent, or not English or French). Set under Settings → API; `en` by default.

monthly_limit.description: The key's own monthly limit and what it used this month (its emails and the campaigns it launched, copies included, queue included). `null` when the key has none — only the workspace quota counts then. Beyond it: `402 key_quota_exceeded`.

emails_sent.description: This month's sends accepted by our provider — campaigns, automations, tests and API together.

emails_in_flight.description: Promised but not yet sent: campaign messages waiting in the queue or being sent, reserved automation sends. Already deducted from `emails_remaining`.

emails_remaining.description: What can still be sent this month: quota − `emails_sent` − `emails_in_flight`, never negative. `null` = unlimited. A send asking for more than this returns `402 quota_exceeded`.

resets_at.description: When the monthly counter resets: the 1st of next month at 00:00 UTC (ISO 8601).

billing.description: The subscription as our payment provider reports it. It explains a `plan` that is not the one being paid for: when a payment fails for good, the workspace runs on the free plan's limits while `subscribed_plan` still names the plan that was bought.

status.description: `none` = never subscribed (free plan, nothing to pay). Otherwise the provider's status: `active`, `trialing`, `past_due` (a payment failed, access kept while it retries), `unpaid` (retries abandoned: free plan limits apply), `canceled`, `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `paused`.

subscribed_plan.description: The plan being billed, while a subscription is alive; `null` otherwise. It can differ from `plan.id` (see `status`).

current_period_end.description: End of the period already paid for; `null` without a live subscription.

cancel_at_period_end.description: `true` when the subscription has been cancelled and stops at the end of the period.

trial_ends_at.description: End of the free week — offered once per workspace, on its first move to a paid plan — when `status` is `trialing`: the plan already applies and the first charge falls on this date (ISO 8601). `null` otherwise.

scheduled_change.description: A change that will take effect later — a downgrade, or a cancellation (`plan: "free"`); `null` if none.

manage_url.description: The billing screen where the owner or an administrator changes plan, card or invoices. In the language of the call (`Accept-Language`).

limits.description: The other limits of the plan, and how much of each is used.

members.description: Seats in the workspace. A pending, unexpired invitation takes a seat.

daily.description: The daily limit of a new workspace, over a rolling 24 hours: 100 emails for the first three days, 500 until the seventh, then none. `null` when it does not apply. A send above it returns `429 daily_quota_exceeded`.

used.description: Accepted over the last 24 hours, plus what is waiting in the queue.

remaining.description: What can still go out now; never negative.

next_limit.description: The next limit (`500`), or `null` when the next step lifts it.

subscribers.description: Subscribers with status `subscribed` — the ones a campaign would reach.

sending_domains.description: The workspace's domains. Only those with `verified: true` can serve as `from`.

senders.description: The registered senders. A CAMPAIGN can only go out from one of them; an individual email, on the other hand, accepts any address on a verified domain.

id.description: To pass as `sender_id` when creating a campaign.

name.description: The name shown in the inbox.

default.description: The one a campaign takes if you designate none.

has_more.description: One more page after this one.

next_cursor.description: To pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

Liste.description: The envelope of every list. To walk through it: as long as `has_more` is `true`, call the same address again with `?cursor=<next_cursor>`. The order is stable; a page returns at most `limit` items (50 by default, 100 at most).

code.description: Write your code against this field, never against `message`.

message.description: Written to be read by a human; may be rephrased without notice.

details.description: What you need to fix things without guessing: `issues` (the offending field and why) on a validation error, `verifiedDomains` on a refused domain, `available` on an unknown sender, and on `quota_exceeded` the numbers `plan`, `quota`, `sent`, `in_flight`, `remaining`, `requested`, `resets_at`, and on `free_plan_domain_used` the `domain`, its `root_domain`, the `period` and `resets_at`, and on `key_quota_exceeded` the key's `key_id`, `key_name`, `limit`, `used`, `remaining`, `requested` and `resets_at`. A `429` and a `423` also give `retry_after_seconds` when the refusal comes from a daily limit or a safety review — the same value as `Retry-After`.

message.description: The same text as `error.message` — written for a human.

name.description: The same value as `error.code`. Write your logic against it.

Erreur.description: Two readings of the same content. `error` is Mailcheer's shape, structured. `statusCode`, `message` and `name` follow Resend's shape, so that code written against that API shows a correct message without being rewritten. `name` carries the same value as `error.code`, and `message` the same text as `error.message`.

error.message: Domain “example.com” is not verified in this workspace. Verified domains: yourdomain.com.

examples.message: Domain “example.com” is not verified in this workspace. Verified domains: yourdomain.com.
examples.name: unverified_from_domain

Carte.description: The API's table of contents, readable without a key.

scopes.description: Every permission a key can carry.

endpoints.description: Each endpoint and the permission it requires.

scope.description: `—` if no particular permission is required.

secret.description: The signing secret (`whsec_…`). Returned on creation, when reading one specific subscription, and after a secret rotation — **never in the list**, which we log in full without a second thought.

url.description: `https` required, and never a private-network address.

event_id.description: Stable across attempts: it is the deduplication key.

response_status.description: The HTTP status code your service returned.

response_body.description: The first 500 characters of its response.

QuotaThresholdEvent.description: The body of a `quota.threshold_reached` call. The same envelope as every event (`id`, `type`, `created_at`, `data`).

threshold.description: The threshold reached, in percent of the monthly quota.

quota.description: Emails a month included in the plan.

in_flight.description: Emails promised but not yet sent (queue).

remaining.description: What can still be sent this month: `quota − sent − in_flight`, never negative.

resets_at.description: When the counter resets: the 1st of next month, 00:00 UTC.

EmailEvent.description: The body of an `email.*` call. A test event carries a different `data`: see `TestEvent`.

id.description: `evt_…` — the same on every attempt and every replay of the event: the deduplication key.

created_at.description: When the event occurred (not when it was delivered).

test.description: Present, and `true`, on an event produced by a test key (`mch_test_…`): the email was simulated, nothing went out. Absent on a real event. `data` is that of a real event.

message_id.description: With `source: api`, the `id` returned by `POST /api/v1/emails`. With `source: campaign`, the `id` of the recipient's row in `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/recipients`.

email.description: The address the event concerns. For a campaign email whose contact was deleted after the send, an empty string.

campaign_id.description: Campaign emails only: the campaign that sent it.

subscriber_id.description: Campaign emails whose contact still exists.

subject.description: The subject of the campaign or of the email, when it has one.

url.description: `email.clicked` only: the link that was clicked.

reason.description: `email.bounced`: the bounce type reported by Amazon SES — `Permanent` (the address does not exist), `Transient`, `Undetermined`. `email.failed`: why the email did not go out — `provider_rejected` (our sending provider refused it), `safety_review` (handed to a human safety review: send the call again after the decision), `suspended` (the workspace was suspended by the review), `interrupted` (a failure before the send).

recipient_type.description: API emails only: `to` if the address was a recipient, `cc` or `bcc` if it was a copy.

EmailReceivedEvent.description: The body of an `email.received` call. A test event carries a different `data`: see `TestEvent`.

id.description: `evt_…` — the same on every attempt and every replay of the event: the deduplication key.

created_at.description: When the event occurred (not when it was delivered).

email.description: The address of the person who replied — the same as `from`, so that `data.email` names the contact in every `email.*` event.

from_name.description: Their display name, when they have one.

to.description: The `reply.<domain>` addresses that received the reply.

cc.description: The visible copy addresses, when there are any.

text.description: The plain-text version, as is (including the quote of your email), when the reply has one.

html.description: The HTML version, as is, when the reply has one. It comes from a stranger: never display it without sanitizing it.

attachments.description: One entry per attachment: `filename`, `content_type`, `size` (bytes), `content_id` (inline image), `url` — a signed download link that needs no key — and `url_expires_at` (7 days). Always present, possibly empty.

message_id.description: When the original email is found: the `id` of the Mailcheer email being replied to, as in the other `email.*` events. Found through the reply address, or through `In-Reply-To` and `References` — never guessed.

source.description: With `message_id`: where the original email came from.

campaign_id.description: Reply to a campaign email: the campaign.

automation_id.description: Reply to an automation email: the automation.

tags.description: Reply to an API email that carried `tags`: those tags, to file the reply on your side.

spam.description: `true` when Amazon's filter judges the reply to be spam.

automatic.description: `true` for an automatic reply: out of office, acknowledgement, delivery report (`Auto-Submitted`, `Precedence`…).

data.subject: Re: Your September invoice
data.text:
Hello, can you send it to our accounting team too?

On 25 Sept 2026, Your company wrote:
> Please find your invoice attached.

SubscriberEvent.description: The body of a `subscriber.*` call. A test event carries a different `data`: see `TestEvent`.

id.description: `evt_…` — the same on every attempt and every replay of the event: the deduplication key.

created_at.description: When the event occurred (not when it was delivered).

source.description: `subscriber.created` only. `form`: a signup form (`pending` until the person confirms). `api`: the API or MCP (`pending`, or `subscribed` with `double_opt_in: false`). `manual`: added in the app.

reason.description: `subscriber.unsubscribed` only: `unsubscribe` (an email's link, `DELETE /api/v1/subscribers/{email}`, the app), or the reason given when the address was added to the suppression list.

campaign_id.description: `subscriber.unsubscribed` through a campaign email's link: the campaign.

message_id.description: `subscriber.unsubscribed` through a campaign email's link: the recipient's row whose link was used.

automation_id.description: `subscriber.unsubscribed` through an automation email's link: the automation.

TestEvent.description: The body of the test event (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`, or Settings → API). Its `type` is the subscription's first event, but its `data` holds only `test` and `message` — **none of the fields of the real event**. Check `data.test === true` before reading anything else, and answer 2xx without processing it.

id.description: `evt_…` — the same on every attempt and every replay of the event: the deduplication key.

created_at.description: When the event occurred (not when it was delivered).

message.description: A sentence in the language of the request (`Accept-Language`) or of the screen.

subscribers.description: Subscribers carrying the tag, every status.

subscribed.description: Among them, the active subscribers — those a campaign would reach.

added.description: Subscribers who received the tag with this call.

unchanged.description: Subscribers found on whom nothing changed (already tagged, or already untagged).

not_found.description: Addresses that are not subscribers of this workspace — nothing is created.

added.description: Tags this call put on the record (it did not have them).

removed.description: Tags this call removed (the record had them).

subscribers.description: 1 to 500 subscribers, each in the form of `POST /api/v1/subscribers`.

data.description: One line per entry, in order. `created` and `updated` carry the fields of `POST /api/v1/subscribers`'s response (`subscriber`, `confirmation_sent`…); `rejected` carries `error` — the refusal the single add would have returned.

suppressed.description: `true` if the address stays on the suppression list — nothing will be sent to it again, even re-imported.

subject.description: The subject. It may stay empty on a draft, but the send will refuse it.

preheader.description: Preview shown after the subject in the inbox.
examples: Three new things, and one we owed you.

kind.description: Your own classification label. Free text, no imposed value.

from.description: The address of a sender **already registered** in the workspace — not any address on a verified domain, unlike an individual send. Unknown: 404, with the list of available addresses. `GET /api/v1/me` gives them in `senders`.

The sender's identifier, if you know it (`senders[].id` from `GET /api/v1/me`). Takes precedence over `from`.

With neither `from` nor `sender_id`, Mailcheer takes the workspace's default sender; failing that, if a single sender exists, that one. If several exist with no default, the campaign is created **without a sender** and it is the send that will fail: designate one.

text.description: The content in plain text — the form to prefer from code or from an agent. A blank line separates two paragraphs, `# ` at the start of a line makes a heading, `## ` a subheading. Ignored if `content` is provided.

Here is what changed this month.

Enjoy the read.

content.description: The content in blocks, the editor's full form. Write this only if you are reusing the content of an existing campaign: to compose, `text` does the same job without your having to fabricate block identifiers.

blocks.description: Editor blocks, each with its `id` and its `type` (`heading`, `text`, …).

CampaignUpdate.description: The fields of `CampaignRequest`, all optional. Unknown fields are refused (`422`): a misspelled field ignored in silence would let the old subject go to the whole list. `content` and `text` together are refused. New content without `preheader` keeps the draft's.

Interdit.description: The key does not have the requested permission, or the workspace cannot send: `sending_blocked` (suspended, blocked or banned — nothing goes out, through any channel), `commitment_required` (the anti-spam commitment is not accepted), `reputation_blocked` (too many bounces or complaints).

Introuvable.description: The object does not exist in this workspace.

Conflit.description: Incompatible state, idempotency key reused with a different body, or an identical request still in progress.

Refuse.description: Malformed field, unverified domain, or recipient on the suppression list.

QuotaAtteint.description:
The send is refused before anything leaves; nothing was sent or queued. Two causes, told apart by `error.code`:

- `quota_exceeded` — the plan's monthly quota does not cover this send. `details` gives the numbers: the plan, its quota, what was sent this month, what is waiting in the queue, what remains, what this call asked for, and when the counter resets.
- `free_plan_domain_used` — the workspace is on the free plan, and the sending domain (or another subdomain of the same registered domain) has already used the free plan this month in another workspace. The free plan applies to a sending domain, not to an account. `details`: `domain`, `root_domain`, `period`, `resets_at`. Upgrading to a paid plan lifts the refusal immediately.
- `key_quota_exceeded` — the workspace still has room, but THIS key reached its own monthly limit (Settings → API). Another key of the workspace can still send. `details`: `key_id`, `key_name`, `limit`, `used`, `remaining`, `requested`, `resets_at`.

error.message: Monthly quota exceeded: the Discovery plan includes 3,000 emails a month; 2,940 have already gone out and 20 are queued. You have 40 emails left this month, and this send needs 250. The counter resets on October 1 at 00:00 UTC. To send more before then, change plan (Settings › Billing).

value.message: Monthly quota exceeded: the Discovery plan includes 3,000 emails a month; 2,940 have already gone out and 20 are queued. You have 40 emails left this month, and this send needs 250. The counter resets on October 1 at 00:00 UTC. To send more before then, change plan (Settings › Billing).
value.name: quota_exceeded

error.message: The free plan is per sending domain, not per account: this domain (news.acme.com, part of acme.com) has already used it this month in another workspace. Upgrade to a paid plan to send from several workspaces, or wait until October 1 at 00:00 UTC.

value.message: The free plan is per sending domain, not per account: this domain (news.acme.com, part of acme.com) has already used it this month in another workspace. Upgrade to a paid plan to send from several workspaces, or wait until October 1 at 00:00 UTC.
value.name: free_plan_domain_used

error.message: Key limit reached: the key “Newsletter” cannot send more than 2,400 emails a month. 2,380 have already gone out or are queued this month, 20 remain, and this send needs 551. Nothing was sent. Its counter resets on October 1 at 00:00 UTC. A key's limit is changed under Settings › API.

TropDAppels.description: More than 600 requests per minute for this key (`rate_limit_exceeded` — a batch of N subscribers counts as N), or a new workspace reached its daily limit (`daily_quota_exceeded`: 100 emails per rolling 24 hours for its first three days, 500 until the seventh). `Retry-After` always says how many seconds to wait.

EnvoiEchoue.description: Our sending provider refused the message.

EnPause.description: `sending_paused` — the workspace is paused for a safety review. Nothing is wrong with the call: send it again after the decision, unchanged. `Retry-After` gives an interval to try again (300 seconds): while the review lasts, the call returns `423` again, and writes nothing.
